entities.summary: Metodija Andonov-Čento was a Macedonian politician, partisan leader and the chairman of the Anti-Fascist Assembly of the National Liberation of Macedonia and first president of the presidency of the people's assembly of the People's Republic of Macedonia in the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia. During the interwar period, he earned a living as a merchant. After World War II, he was persecuted by the Yugoslav Macedonian authorities for his desire to establish an independent Macedonia. The persona of Čento was a taboo in Yugoslav Macedonia, but it was rehabilitated during the 1990s, after the country gained its independence.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the first president of the presidency of the people's assembly of the People's Republic of Macedonia, Čento played a crucial role in shaping Yugoslavia's political landscape after World War II. His persecution by Yugoslav authorities and subsequent rehabilitation highlight the complexities of Macedonian identity during the Cold War era.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As chairman of the Anti-Fascist Assembly and first president of the presidency of the people's assembly, Čento played a crucial role in shaping Macedonia's post-war politics. His persecution by Yugoslav authorities for advocating Macedonian independence had significant regional implications.
